### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d79eecfe5b78598f9117726b542615ca2332d58f`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (literal, 56 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d79eecfe5b78598f9117726b542615ca2332d58f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `497170c2e0c081b9595f6ace8a9542edd7b04512` — the merge of head `c745679c608b987d8810d2b3a2c4b27e03991d62` into base `d79eecfe5b78598f9117726b542615ca2332d58f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 497170c2e0c081b9595f6ace8a9542edd7b04512 && git checkout 497170c2e0c081b9595f6ace8a9542edd7b04512
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d79eecfe5b78598f9117726b542615ca2332d58f c745679c608b987d8810d2b3a2c4b27e03991d62 && git checkout -B drift-repro d79eecfe5b78598f9117726b542615ca2332d58f && git merge --no-ff c745679c608b987d8810d2b3a2c4b27e03991d62

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d79eecfe5b78598f9117726b542615ca2332d58f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d79eecfe5b78598f9117726b542615ca2332d58f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c745679c608b987d8810d2b3a2c4b27e03991d62`
Local-runs: none
Scope: card #30023 body and all three comments (triage 6625679577, Claim 6629587477, dev report 6630951308); the seat order `/mnt/project-files/server-orders/30023.md`; the dev report and replacement body under `/mnt/project-files/issue-30023/` against the live PR body (identical); `git diff origin/main...pr-30084` in full (two linear commits, 10 files, +710/−44); PR #30021's delta review 6625831334 and its merged changeset `.changeset/29896-field-sortable-false-honoured.md` (140d8ce8); precedent #9257 and its PM review; `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (`already-registered` branch), `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (arm reader), AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3; `resolveObjectSortability` / `fieldEntriesOf` (`sortability.zod.ts`), `walkPageComponents` (`page-walk.ts`), `ObjectSearchTarget` (`validate-searchable-fields.ts`), `validateReferenceIntegrity` dispatch and `DEFAULT_MEMBER_RUNTIME_TYPES`, `runtime-gate.ts:1178`, the per-write snapshot in `protocol-authoring-gate.ts`; the spec `sort:` keys in `component.zod.ts` / `page.zod.ts`; the UI consumers of each walked slot (`element-data-source.ts`, `recordBinding.tsx`, `record-related-list.tsx`, `recordPagePayload.ts`, `LineItemsPanel.tsx`, `ObjectGrid/Calendar/Gantt/Map/Timeline.tsx`, `plugin-list/index.tsx`, `InterfaceListPage.tsx:503`, `PageView.tsx`); `validate-page-field-bindings.ts`; `liveness/page.json`; the 23 Supersedes precedents in changeset history; the head's 64 check-runs.

Face: a narrowing of the publish gate. `validate-sortable-fields` now judges a stored sort by `resolveObjectSortability`'s projection for both reasons, so a sort naming a field declared `sortable: false` is `sort-field-unsortable` at `error` on the five list-view rungs it already walked; it newly walks every stored page sort (block `sort`, element `dataSource.sort`, `parentDataSource.sort`, `interfaceConfig.sort`, `record.sort`) for the projection's verdict only, which also refuses a `formula` sort on those page slots for the first time; `validateReferenceIntegrity` dispatches on a `page` write for this one member. `protocol.ts` / `engine.ts` untouched; no facade row owed.

### ① Derived judgments
- **Same projection as the door, both reasons, at the #9257 level.** `unsortableFinding` reads `projection[name].sortable === false` and branches on `reason === FIELD_UNSORTABLE_AUTHOR_DECLARED`; the projection is `resolveObjectSortability(obj).fields` over the authored object (`indexObjectSortability`), the resolver `assertSortFieldsExist` refuses by. The virtual message is byte-identical to before; the author-declared message carries the door's clause (`a field on object "X" that declares \`sortable: false\``). Both `error`, the level #9257 landed (`validate-sortable-fields` has always been `error`; triage and the PM review on #9257 ruled it). A `formula` field also marked `false` keeps `virtual-type` because the projection does (pinned on the view and on a page).
- **The second narrowing (virtual sorts on page slots) is real and declared.** Before, no page sort was judged for sortability at all, so a page `formula` sort published green. The Clause-② line says "where a `formula` sort is now refused too", the Before bullet names it, and a lint pin plus a route control cover it. Same kind (`narrowed`), one arm; nothing extra owed.
- **Every walked surface reaches the data door.** `dataSource.sort` → `element-data-source.ts:503` composes `config.sort ?? view.sort` into the read; `parentDataSource.sort` → `ParentRecordBinding` (`recordBinding.tsx:515` `$orderby`); `record:related_list` `sort` → `recordPagePayload.ts:169` → `related[].sort` → `findData`; `record:line_items` `sort` → `LineItemsPanel.tsx:400` `convertSortToQueryParams(schema.sort)`; `object-grid/calendar/gantt/map/timeline` `sort` → each renderer's `$orderby: convertSortToQueryParams(schema.sort)`; page `list-view` → `ListViewRenderer` (a list view's own sort); `interfaceConfig.sort` → `InterfaceListPage.tsx:503`; app page `record.sort` → `PageView.tsx:236` `$orderby`. No false-refusal surface. The `PAGE_BLOCK_SORT_OBJECT_PROP` table equals the live `sort:` keys of `ComponentPropsMap` (seven `sort:` declarations plus `ListViewPageProps`' spread; `element:record_picker` / `element:repeater` are tombstones), and that equality is pinned with a non-vacuity control.
- **No missed surface.** Dashboard `sortBy` and report `order[].by` are dataset names (as #9257 settled); `kind: 'react'` pages are `validate-react-page-props`' (and `walkPageComponents` already skips them). Nothing else under `packages/spec/src/ui` carries an object-field sort.
- **Binding precedence matches the renderers.** `elementDataSourceBlock` maps `dataSource.object` onto the block's object key, so a block `sort` is judged against `dataSource.object ?? <block prop>`; `interfaceConfig.source ?? page.object` matches `InterfaceListPage`. An object from another package has no projection and is skipped (no refusal on an unresolvable binding).
- **The page door crossing is real and pinned through the real route.** `validateReferenceIntegrity` filters members by `options.runtimeWriteType` (`runtime-gate.ts:1178` sets it to the written type); members without `runtimeTypes` default to `['flow']`, and `validateSortableFields` is the only member naming `page`, so a page write runs exactly one member. The per-write snapshot gathers `objects` on every write (`protocol-authoring-gate.ts` `listCollection('object', 'objects')`), so the member has its universe and no missing-collection channel. Pinned at `saveMetaItem({ type: 'page' })` on the stub-engine harness: 422 `INVALID_METADATA` at the four slot paths, nothing stored; the view door likewise; the dispatch roster pin lists `validateReferenceIntegrity`. Ablation B (drop `page`) reds exactly the 4 page slots plus the page virtual control; ablation A (author-declared guard off) reds the 7 author-declared cases and the 5 route refusals, controls green. Reported, not re-run here.
- **Exported core stays compatible.** `checkSortDeclaration`'s new trailing `sortability` is optional; absent, the projection is derived from `ObjectSearchTarget.fields`, which carries `type`/`hidden`/`searchable` and no `sortable`, so an out-of-repo caller gets the virtual-only answer, as pinned. `validate-sortable-fields.ts` is the only in-repo caller.
- **Entry text matches the code.** `surface` lists exactly the eight blocks in the table plus the four other slots; `acceptanceCriteria` is phrased as the `os validate` finding; the "Lint does not yet judge" sentence is replaced truthfully (the page door now dispatches). The committed `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` carries neither 18.x entry on main, so it lags unreleased entries by design; no regeneration owed.
- **Corpus.** No shipped object declares `sortable: false`; the rule gives 0 findings over the four example apps, and the all-fields-`false` probe fires on two showcase `interfaceConfig.sort` slots, so the page walk is live on real metadata. Reported.

### ② Semver level
`@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/spec` both `minor`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` with one arm; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; BREAKING banner with Before / Now / Not changed / The remedy. Judged the same: a metadata value refused is `narrowed`, which takes at least `minor` on each moved package. "The widening half:" is prose after the arm, not a parenthetical, so `readClause2Line` reads one arm (the identical spelling in #30021's changeset passed). No `FROM → TO` label is owed: AGENTS.md ties that mapping to removing or renaming an authorable thing, nothing is removed here, and #30021 (140d8ce8) landed the same class with Before/Now/Remedy and no literal label. ADR-0087: `not-required (already-registered field-sortable-false-sort-refused)` is valid. The id resolves at HEAD and existed at the merge base (140d8ce8 is an ancestor of c23501b2), the `why` clears 40 characters, and the branch `continue`s before the prescription-contradiction check, so "**The remedy.**" is allowed; `registered` would be refused by R4 as the dev says, and #9257 used this very category (`already-registered engine-find-formula-order-by-refused`). Supersedes paragraph: the bolded "**Supersedes, in the same release.**" form is the repo's established shape (the #29904, #27008, #26660 notes), the superseded note is still in `.changeset/` on main (unreleased; last version-packages commit predates 140d8ce8) and does contain "Lint does not yet judge these at authoring." Skills-docs `none — REASON` is in the closed vocabulary.

### ③ Boundary flags
- CI at head: 64 check-runs, 55 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed (Test Core 8/8, Test UI 16/16, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, all lint and type-check gates, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness).
- Existence on page sorts is uneven and pre-existing: `validate-page-field-bindings` reads block `sort` and `interfaceConfig.sort` (at `warning`), but nothing reads element `dataSource.sort` or an app page `record.sort` for an unknown name; that name reaches the door and answers 400. Out of this card's scope (the order confined it to the sortability verdict); the dev's class-b finding covers the severity half only.
- The object publish door does not run `validateSortableFields` (member lacks `object`; the `reference-integrity-suite.ts` note reserves that crossing), so an object write carrying `sortable: false` and a built-in `listViews.*.sort` on the same field saves and fails at read; `os validate` catches it. Pre-existing, reported by the dev.
- `liveness/page.json` grades every `props.record.*` row `planned` while `PageView.tsx#appPageRecordBinding` reads `record.sort`; stale ledger, not moved here.
- Nit, not owed: a block carrying both `dataSource.sort` and its own `sort` has the binding override the block's (`element-data-source.ts` "binding overrides view"), so the inert `properties.sort` is still judged. The list-view rungs already behave this way; consistent.

### ④ Narrowing face
- `validate-sortable-fields.ts`: one projection, two messages, `error`; the page walk uses the shared `walkPageComponents` (cycle-safe, source-authored pages skipped) and asks only the sortability question, so no name is reported twice.
- `reference-integrity-suite.ts` / `authoring-rules.ts`: `page` on the member and on the suite entry; the entry's rationale comment names the one member a page write reaches.
- `18.field-sortable-false-sort-refused.ts`: surface, reason and acceptance criteria widened to the full stored list; shape unchanged.
- Changeset and PR body: identical declarations; disposition verified; Supersedes paragraph true of the unreleased #29896 note.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-vyggze`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

Verdict: **ACCEPT** at head `c745679c608b987d8810d2b3a2c4b27e03991d62` · 2026-11-04T13:11Z

- **Shape:**
  - `validate-sortable-fields` judges a stored sort by `resolveObjectSortability`'s projection for both reasons. A sort naming a field declared `sortable: false` is `sort-field-unsortable` at `error` on the five list-view rungs.
  - The rule newly walks every stored page sort (block `sort`, element `dataSource.sort`, `parentDataSource.sort`, `interfaceConfig.sort`, `record.sort`) for the projection's verdict only, which also refuses a `formula` sort on those slots.
  - `validateReferenceIntegrity` dispatches on a `page` write for this one member, pinned through the real `saveMetaItem` route.
  - The `18.field-sortable-false-sort-refused` entry's surface text is widened to the full stored list.
- **Review:** the `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review at this head is PASS (record above).
- **Premise measured:** before/after on the lint and route pins. Ablations: A, the author-declared guard turned off (7 cases + 5 route refusals red); B, `page` dropped from `runtimeTypes` (4 page slots + the virtual control red). Each was red, then restored. The corpus gives 0 findings over the four example apps, and an all-`false` probe fires on two showcase `interfaceConfig.sort` slots.
- **Declaration:** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, minor on `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/spec`, BREAKING with Before / Now / Not changed / The remedy, `adr-0087: not-required (already-registered field-sortable-false-sort-refused)`, and a Supersedes paragraph for #29896's pending note. Reviewed as correct. No `FROM → TO` label is owed, because nothing authorable is removed or renamed (the same class as #30021).
- **CI (head):** 64 check-runs, 55 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed.
- **Accepted deviations:** the harness-pinned branch `claude/project-thread-vyggze`. The seat files three follow-ups:
  - existence readers and severity for page sorts (element `dataSource.sort`, app page `record.sort`);
  - the `liveness/page.json` `props.record.*` regrade;
  - the object publish door not dispatching `validateSortableFields`.

  A nit is carried: the Supersedes paragraph could name the superseded file.
- **Landing:** on all-green at this head, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay. It closes #30023.
